chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Running the Clef Club as a nonprofit bottle club
summary: Horace and his wife ran the after-hours club for a corporation headed by attorney Robert Carr, in the old Arthur Murray studio, a bottle club sponsored by the Rudinsky Foundation, hosting Stan Kenton's birthday.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And you took over. You were running that.
Yes, my wife and I ran that club for the corporation that owned it, and we were part of that corporation. In fact, the gentleman that was president of the corporation was --
-- an attorney here named Robert Carr.

-- former governor of Colorado. And Bob Carr's quite a guy. And we ran the thing seven nights a week, and it's a haven for musicians that would come into town, like Stan Kenton and his great band. In fact, Stan was here; the night of
his birthday we gave him a big birthday party in this club. This club, incidentally, was formerly the old Arthur Murray --
-- dancing upstairs. We remodeled the thing, and it was a nonprofit organization, and it was -- that's the only way we could run. sponsored (unintelligible) on after hours.
Bottle club. The -- it was sponsored by the Rudinsky Foundation here in Denver. And it was a bottle club. (Unintelligible). The only thing you could do was serve setups.

And you had your own bottle labeled (unintelligible) lock up the bottles, and when you come in, you had your card. You were a member, all you do is ask for your bottle. And you would be given your bottle and served your setups. Give me my bottle -- serve yourself. And we had some of the greatest performers ever there.
